spec.description: TriMet's real-time dashboard (Portland) on the Kepler Plus fleet layer, every panel answered in the browser by Chaski: punctuality, service changes and alerts.

options.content:
### TriMet in real time, Portland, Oregon — fleet edition

TriMet's live dashboard rebuilt on two of our own pieces: the **Fleet** layer of Kepler Plus and **Chaski**, DuckDB in your browser. Every vehicle TriMet is tracking right now, how late it runs, which trips skip stops and what riders are being warned about. **On time** follows TriMet's own yardstick: from one minute early to five minutes late.

On every refresh the server reads each TriMet feed once, through a 15 s cache that also adds the API key, and hands the rows to Chaski; the routes and stops load once per visit. From there every panel is answered in your browser: the filters at the top — **mode, route, punctuality and traffic** — recompute the whole page without going back to the server (punctuality and traffic only narrow the maps). Nothing is stored, so there is no history.

On the map each vehicle is a fleet asset, drawn as a 3D model of its kind — bus, MAX train or WES train — with a beacon in the colour of its punctuality: turned to its heading, it glides to its new position on each refresh, and the map remembers its last positions to draw the trail behind it — the feed itself only brings the latest one. Keep the page open for a few refreshes to see the trails grow. **Click a vehicle**, or a row of the delayed table, and the *Vehicle cam* rides behind it.

<small>Data: TriMet Web Services. Unofficial dashboard, not endorsed by or affiliated with TriMet. TriMet and TransitTracker are registered trademarks of TriMet.</small>

spec.rawSql:
SELECT CASE WHEN load_pct IS NULL THEN 'Not reported'
            WHEN load_pct < 25     THEN 'Under 25 %'
            WHEN load_pct < 50     THEN '25–50 %'
            WHEN load_pct < 70     THEN '50–70 %'
            WHEN load_pct < 90     THEN '70–90 %'
            ELSE '90 % or more' END      AS "Load",
       count(*)::BIGINT                  AS "Buses"
FROM $vehicles
WHERE mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route IN ($route))
  AND type = 'bus'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY min(coalesce(load_pct, 1000))

spec.description: Buses by the share of capacity they report being used (an experimental TriMet field; trains do not report it, and some buses do not either).
spec.title: How full the buses are

spec.rawSql:
-- The fleet within the four filters, as on the main map; the camera follows
-- $vehicle, written by a click on either map or a row of the delayed table.
SELECT v.vehicle, v.vehicle AS unit, v.route, v.mode, v.type, v.sign, v.punctuality,
       v.delay_min, s.name AS next_stop, v.load_pct, v.in_traffic, v.age_s,
       v.heading, v.latitude, v.longitude, v.time
FROM $vehicles v LEFT JOIN $stops s ON s.locid = v.next_loc
WHERE mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route IN ($route))
    AND ('__all__' IN ($punctuality) OR punctuality IN ($punctuality))
    AND ('__all__' IN ($in_traffic) OR in_traffic IN ($in_traffic))

spec.description: The camera rides behind the vehicle clicked on the main map or picked in the delayed table, facing its heading, and follows it on every refresh. Click another vehicle, here or on the main map, to switch. Dragging pauses the camera for ten seconds; the chip at the top switches between chase, orbit and follow.
spec.title: Vehicle cam — the vehicle clicked on the map

spec.rawSql:
WITH v AS (SELECT * FROM $vehicles WHERE mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route IN ($route)))
SELECT
  -- About the feed, so it reads the unfiltered rows.
  (SELECT round((epoch_ms(now()) - max(feed_ms)) / 1000.0)::BIGINT FROM $vehicles) AS "Feed age",
  count(*)::BIGINT                                                     AS "Vehicles in service",
  100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE delay_s BETWEEN -60 AND 300) / nullif(count(*), 0) AS "On time",
  median(delay_s) / 60.0                                               AS "Median delay",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE delay_s > 300)::BIGINT                        AS "More than 5 min late",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE delay_s < -60)::BIGINT                        AS "More than 1 min early",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE in_traffic = 'Congested')::BIGINT             AS "Stuck in traffic",
  quantile_cont(age_s, 0.9)                                            AS "Position age (p90)"
FROM v

spec.description: Vehicles reporting a position on a route, after the mode and route filters. Feed age: how long ago TriMet answered, over every vehicle. On time: between 1 minute early and 5 minutes late, TriMet's definition. Stuck in traffic: buses reporting that they are not moving in congestion (an experimental TriMet field). Position age: 90 % of positions are younger than this.
spec.title: Service right now

spec.rawSql:
WITH t AS (SELECT * FROM $trips WHERE mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route IN ($route)))
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE canceled > 0)::BIGINT AS "Trips with canceled stops"
FROM t

spec.description: Trips running now or starting within the hour with at least one canceled stop — detours, closures, short turns.
spec.title: Trips skipping stops

spec.rawSql:
-- Only what the fleet layer and the tooltip read, within the four filters.
SELECT v.vehicle, v.vehicle AS unit, v.route, v.mode, v.type, v.sign, v.punctuality,
       v.delay_min, s.name AS next_stop, v.load_pct, v.in_traffic, v.age_s,
       v.heading, v.latitude, v.longitude, v.time
FROM $vehicles v LEFT JOIN $stops s ON s.locid = v.next_loc
WHERE mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route IN ($route))
    AND ('__all__' IN ($punctuality) OR punctuality IN ($punctuality))
    AND ('__all__' IN ($in_traffic) OR in_traffic IN ($in_traffic))

-- The routes in their public colours, within the mode and route filters.
SELECT route AS line, mode AS kind, color, width, geojson
FROM $routes
WHERE mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route IN ($route))

-- Stops named in an alert, within the route filter, like the alerts table.
SELECT alert, affects, stop, latitude, longitude
FROM $alert_stops
WHERE '__all__' IN ($route)
   OR id IN (SELECT id FROM $alert_routes WHERE route IN ($route))

-- The vehicle picked on the map or in the delayed table, so the ring follows
-- it on every refresh. Empty until then, which matches nothing.
SELECT latitude, longitude, vehicle AS picked
FROM $vehicles
WHERE vehicle = $vehicle

-- Where each vehicle is headed: from where it is now to its next two stops,
-- drawn as arrows. Only stops TriMet expects it at within five minutes, where
-- the estimate is freshest and the arrow stays close to its bus. A vehicle
-- that has not served a stop of its trip yet is on its way to the terminal or
-- on layover, and a line from it to the first stop would not be a route, so
-- it gets no arrow; nor does one silent for two minutes. A MAX train is two
-- cars on one trip, and one arrow is enough. Within the same four filters as
-- the vehicles.
WITH veh AS (
  SELECT trip, route, latitude AS lat, longitude AS lng, feed_ms AS qt
  FROM $vehicles
  WHERE last_seq IS NOT NULL AND age_s < 120
    AND mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route IN ($route))
    AND ('__all__' IN ($punctuality) OR punctuality IN ($punctuality))
    AND ('__all__' IN ($in_traffic) OR in_traffic IN ($in_traffic))
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY trip ORDER BY time DESC) = 1
),
ahead AS (
  SELECT v.trip, u.seq, u.locid
  FROM $tripstops u JOIN veh v ON v.trip = u.trip
  WHERE u.status <> 'canceled'
    AND coalesce(u.adjusted_ms, u.aimed_ms) > v.qt
    AND coalesce(u.adjusted_ms, u.aimed_ms) <= v.qt + 300000
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY v.trip ORDER BY u.seq) <= 2
),
pts AS (
  SELECT trip, 0 AS seq, lat, lng FROM veh WHERE trip IN (SELECT trip FROM ahead)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT a.trip, a.seq, s.lat, s.lng FROM ahead a JOIN $stops s ON s.locid = a.locid
),
hop AS (
  SELECT trip, lat, lng, lead(lat) OVER w AS lat1, lead(lng) OVER w AS lng1
  FROM pts WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY trip ORDER BY seq)
)
SELECT h.lat  AS origin_lat,
       h.lng  AS origin_lng,
       h.lat1 AS dest_lat,
       h.lng1 AS dest_lng,
       count(*)::BIGINT   AS trips,
       any_value(v.route) AS route
FROM hop h JOIN veh v USING (trip)
WHERE h.lat1 IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4

spec.description: Each vehicle from TriMet's vehicle feed is a fleet asset: a 3D model of a bus, a MAX train or a WES train, turned to the heading it reports and topped by a beacon, gliding to its new position on every refresh, with a trail of where it went over the last minutes — remembered by the map while the page stays open. Blue: more than a minute early; green: on time; amber: 5–10 minutes late; red: later. Lines are the routes in their public colours, drawn stop to stop rather than along the street. Amber rings are stops named in a service alert, and the cyan ring the selected vehicle. Click a vehicle to follow it in the Vehicle cam and list its next stops. Moving arrows run from each vehicle to its next two stops, where TriMet expects it within five minutes.
spec.title: Fleet now — colored by punctuality

config.label: Stops named in a service alert
Next two stops of each vehicle

spec.rawSql:
SELECT v.route                      AS "Route",
       v.vehicle                    AS "Vehicle",
       v.sign                       AS "Headsign",
       v.delay_min                  AS "Late (min)",
       coalesce(s.name, '')         AS "Next stop",
       -- Text, not numbers: a data link interpolates the cell's formatted
       -- value, and the table's automatic decimals would round the position.
       printf('%.6f', v.latitude)   AS center_lat,
       printf('%.6f', v.longitude)  AS center_lng
FROM $vehicles v LEFT JOIN $stops s ON s.locid = v.next_loc
WHERE mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route IN ($route))
  AND v.delay_s > 60
ORDER BY v.delay_s DESC
LIMIT 25

spec.description: The 25 vehicles furthest behind schedule. Click a row to follow it in the Vehicle cam, find it on the map and list its next stops.
spec.title: Most delayed vehicles now

links.title: Follow it and list its next stops

spec.rawSql:
-- $vehicle is written by a click on the map or on the delayed table; empty
-- until then, which matches nothing. The trip it is running, stop by stop.
SELECT coalesce(s.name, u.locid::VARCHAR)    AS "Stop",
       to_timestamp(u.aimed_ms / 1000)       AS "Scheduled",
       to_timestamp(u.adjusted_ms / 1000)    AS "Expected",
       round(u.delay_s / 60.0, 1)            AS "Late (min)",
       CASE u.status WHEN 'canceled' THEN 'Canceled'
                     WHEN 'dropOffOnly' THEN 'Drop-off only'
                     ELSE '' END             AS "Note"
FROM $tripstops u LEFT JOIN $stops s ON s.locid = u.locid
WHERE u.trip IN (SELECT trip FROM $vehicles WHERE vehicle = $vehicle)
ORDER BY u.seq

spec.description: From TriMet's trip status feed for the trip the selected vehicle is running. Late: minutes behind the scheduled arrival at that stop. Empty until a vehicle is picked.
spec.title: Next stops of the selected vehicle

defaults.noValue: Click a vehicle on the map

spec.rawSql:
SELECT route                                                             AS "Route",
       mode                                                              AS "Mode",
       count(*)::BIGINT                                                  AS "Vehicles",
       100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE delay_s BETWEEN -60 AND 300) / count(*) AS "On time",
       round(median(delay_s) / 60.0, 1)                                  AS "Median late (min)",
       round(max(delay_s) / 60.0, 1)                                     AS "Worst (min)"
FROM $vehicles
WHERE mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route IN ($route))
GROUP BY route, mode
ORDER BY "On time", "Median late (min)" DESC

spec.description: Per route, from the vehicles on it right now. On time: from 1 minute early to 5 minutes late.
spec.title: Routes by punctuality — worst first

spec.rawSql:
WITH t AS (SELECT * FROM $trips WHERE mode IN ($mode)
    AND ('__all__' IN ($route) OR route IN ($route)))
SELECT t.route                                   AS "Route",
       t.destination                             AS "To",
       to_timestamp(t.begin_ms / 1000)           AS "Starts",
       t.canceled::BIGINT                        AS "Canceled stops",
       t.n_stops::BIGINT                         AS "Of",
       coalesce(s.name, '')                      AS "First canceled",
       CASE WHEN t.canceled = t.n_stops THEN 'Canceled'
            WHEN t.extra THEN 'Extra' ELSE '' END AS "Trip"
FROM t LEFT JOIN $stops s ON s.locid = t.first_canceled
WHERE t.canceled > 0
ORDER BY t.begin_ms

spec.description: Trips running now or starting within the hour that will not serve one or more of their stops, from TriMet's trip status feed. Canceled: every stop is skipped. Extra: a trip added outside the published schedule.
spec.title: Service changes — trips skipping stops

spec.rawSql:
-- Follows the route filter; system-wide alerts always show.
SELECT CASE WHEN system_wide THEN 'System-wide' ELSE routes END AS "Routes",
       alert                                                     AS "Alert",
       to_timestamp(since_ms / 1000)                             AS "Since",
       n_stops::BIGINT                                           AS "Stops"
FROM $alerts
WHERE system_wide
   OR '__all__' IN ($route)
   OR id IN (SELECT id FROM $alert_routes WHERE route IN ($route))
ORDER BY since_ms DESC

spec.description: Alerts in effect now, newest first. Follows the route filter; system-wide alerts always show.
spec.title: Active service alerts

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: TriMet wants an AppID, which no browser may see, so DuckDB in
-- the grafana container reads it through the gateway, which adds the key and
-- keeps each answer 15 s (see gateway/feeds.conf); every panel then filters
-- these rows in the browser. One row per vehicle; `vehicle` is the fleet
-- layer's asset and `time` its ping, so the map remembers each vehicle's last
-- positions across refreshes and draws its trail. Not `vehicle_id`: the panel
-- would read that as a trip.
-- One request per feed: read_text fetches the whole answer at once, and the
-- JSON is parsed from memory. The gateway hands it over gunzipped, with no
-- length, ETag or ranges, so there is nothing to read in passes and nothing
-- to check against a renewed cache. (http_get takes five times as long over
-- the 11 MB trip status.) The other TriMet datasets read it the same way.
WITH feed AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT from_json((SELECT content FROM read_text('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/vehicles')),
                   '{"resultSet": {"queryTime": "BIGINT", "vehicle": [{"vehicleID": "BIGINT", "routeNumber": "BIGINT", "routeSubType": "VARCHAR", "tripID": "VARCHAR", "signMessageLong": "VARCHAR", "delay": "BIGINT", "loadPercentage": "BIGINT", "inCongestion": "BOOLEAN", "nextLocID": "BIGINT", "lastStopSeq": "BIGINT", "latitude": "DOUBLE", "longitude": "DOUBLE", "bearing": "BIGINT", "time": "BIGINT"}]}}').resultSet AS rs
),
veh AS (SELECT rs.queryTime AS qt, unnest(rs.vehicle) AS v FROM feed),
routes AS (
  SELECT r.route AS num, r."desc" AS route, r.routeSubType AS subtype
  FROM (SELECT unnest(from_json((SELECT content FROM read_text('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true')),
                                '{"resultSet": {"route": [{"route": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR", "routeSubType": "VARCHAR"}]}}').resultSet.route) AS r)
)
SELECT v.vehicleID::VARCHAR                       AS vehicle,
       v.routeNumber                              AS num,
       coalesce(r.route, v.routeNumber::VARCHAR)  AS route,
       CASE v.routeSubType WHEN 'Light Rail' THEN 'MAX light rail' WHEN 'BRT' THEN 'FX bus rapid transit' WHEN 'Commuter Rail' THEN 'WES commuter rail' WHEN 'Streetcar' THEN 'Streetcar' WHEN 'Aerial Tram' THEN 'Aerial tram' ELSE 'Bus' END AS mode,
       -- Picks the 3D model: a bus, a tram for MAX (light rail) and a train
       -- for WES (commuter rail).
       CASE v.routeSubType WHEN 'Light Rail' THEN 'light rail' WHEN 'Commuter Rail' THEN 'commuter rail'
                           WHEN 'Streetcar' THEN 'streetcar' WHEN 'Aerial Tram' THEN 'aerial tram' ELSE 'bus' END AS type,
       v.tripID                                   AS trip,
       v.signMessageLong                          AS sign,
       -- TriMet counts a late vehicle as negative; flipped so late is positive,
       -- as in GTFS and in TriMet's own trip status feed.
       -v.delay                                   AS delay_s,
       round(-v.delay / 60.0, 1)                  AS delay_min,
       -- TriMet's yardstick: on time is from one minute early to five late.
       CASE WHEN -v.delay < -60  THEN 'Early > 1 min'
            WHEN -v.delay <= 300 THEN 'On time'
            WHEN -v.delay <= 600 THEN 'Late 5–10 min'
            ELSE 'Late > 10 min' END              AS punctuality,
       v.loadPercentage                           AS load_pct,
       CASE WHEN v.inCongestion THEN 'Congested' WHEN NOT v.inCongestion THEN 'Clear' END AS in_traffic,
       v.nextLocID                                AS next_loc,
       v.lastStopSeq                              AS last_seq,
       v.bearing::DOUBLE                          AS heading,
       v.latitude,
       v.longitude,
       to_timestamp(v.time / 1000.0)              AS time,
       round((qt - v.time) / 1000.0)::BIGINT      AS age_s,
       qt                                         AS feed_ms
FROM veh LEFT JOIN routes r ON r.num = v.routeNumber
WHERE v.latitude IS NOT NULL

spec.label: Trips running or due within the hour
spec.name: trips

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: TriMet's trip status, 11 MB of JSON (1 MB as the gateway
-- keeps it), one row per trip, with the stops it will not serve already
-- counted here: the browser gets a thousand rows, not every stop.
WITH feed AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT from_json((SELECT content FROM read_text('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/tripStatus?showRoutes=false')),
                   '{"resultSet": {"queryTime": "BIGINT", "trip": [{"tripID": "VARCHAR", "routeNumber": "VARCHAR", "destination": "VARCHAR", "extraTrip": "BOOLEAN", "tripBeginTime": "BIGINT", "tripEndTime": "BIGINT", "stop": [{"locid": "BIGINT", "stopSequence": "BIGINT", "isPassed": "BOOLEAN", "aimedArrival": "BIGINT", "adjustedArrival": "BIGINT", "arrivalDelay": "BIGINT", "status": "VARCHAR"}]}]}}').resultSet AS rs
),
-- The feed also carries hundreds of trips that ended hours or months ago;
-- kept are those running now or starting within the hour, and a trip
-- scheduled to have ended less than an hour ago (a late bus is still out
-- there).
t AS (
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT rs.queryTime AS qt, unnest(rs.trip) AS t FROM feed)
  WHERE t.tripEndTime >= qt - 3600000 AND t.tripBeginTime <= qt + 3600000
),
routes AS (
  SELECT r.route AS num, r."desc" AS route, r.routeSubType AS subtype
  FROM (SELECT unnest(from_json((SELECT content FROM read_text('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true')),
                                '{"resultSet": {"route": [{"route": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR", "routeSubType": "VARCHAR"}]}}').resultSet.route) AS r)
)
SELECT t.tripID                                              AS trip,
       coalesce(r.route, t.routeNumber)                      AS route,
       CASE r.subtype WHEN 'Light Rail' THEN 'MAX light rail' WHEN 'BRT' THEN 'FX bus rapid transit' WHEN 'Commuter Rail' THEN 'WES commuter rail' WHEN 'Streetcar' THEN 'Streetcar' WHEN 'Aerial Tram' THEN 'Aerial tram' ELSE 'Bus' END AS mode,
       t.destination,
       t.extraTrip                                           AS extra,
       t.tripBeginTime                                       AS begin_ms,
       len(t.stop)                                           AS n_stops,
       len(list_filter(t.stop, s -> s.status = 'canceled'))  AS canceled,
       list_filter(t.stop, s -> s.status = 'canceled')[1].locid AS first_canceled
FROM t LEFT JOIN routes r ON r.num = try_cast(t.routeNumber AS BIGINT)

-- Server side: the next fifteen stops of each trip, from the same feed as
-- the trips: the selected vehicle's next stops and every vehicle's arrows.
WITH feed AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT from_json((SELECT content FROM read_text('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/tripStatus?showRoutes=false')),
                   '{"resultSet": {"queryTime": "BIGINT", "trip": [{"tripID": "VARCHAR", "routeNumber": "VARCHAR", "destination": "VARCHAR", "extraTrip": "BOOLEAN", "tripBeginTime": "BIGINT", "tripEndTime": "BIGINT", "stop": [{"locid": "BIGINT", "stopSequence": "BIGINT", "isPassed": "BOOLEAN", "aimedArrival": "BIGINT", "adjustedArrival": "BIGINT", "arrivalDelay": "BIGINT", "status": "VARCHAR"}]}]}}').resultSet AS rs
),
-- The feed also carries hundreds of trips that ended hours or months ago;
-- kept are those running now or starting within the hour, and a trip
-- scheduled to have ended less than an hour ago (a late bus is still out
-- there).
t AS (
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT rs.queryTime AS qt, unnest(rs.trip) AS t FROM feed)
  WHERE t.tripEndTime >= qt - 3600000 AND t.tripBeginTime <= qt + 3600000
),
s AS (SELECT t.tripID AS trip, unnest(t.stop) AS s FROM t)
SELECT trip,
       s.stopSequence     AS seq,
       s.locid,
       s.aimedArrival     AS aimed_ms,
       s.adjustedArrival  AS adjusted_ms,
       s.arrivalDelay     AS delay_s,
       s.status
FROM s
WHERE NOT s.isPassed
QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY trip ORDER BY s.stopSequence) <= 15

-- Server side: the alerts in effect now, one row each. The routes they name
-- are in alert_routes, the stops in alert_stops: one row per route or stop,
-- since the browser gets rows, not lists.
WITH feed AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT from_json((SELECT content FROM read_text('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/alerts')),
                   '{"resultSet": {"alert": [{"id": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR", "begin": "BIGINT", "system_wide_flag": "BOOLEAN", "route": [{"route": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR"}], "location": [{"id": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR", "lat": "DOUBLE", "lng": "DOUBLE"}]}]}}').resultSet AS rs
),
al AS (SELECT unnest(rs.alert) AS a FROM feed)
SELECT a.id,
       trim(a."desc", chr(10) || ' ')                                                  AS alert,
       a.begin                                                                         AS since_ms,
       coalesce(a.system_wide_flag, false)                                             AS system_wide,
       array_to_string(list_sort(list_distinct(list_transform(a.route, x -> x."desc"))), ', ') AS routes,
       coalesce(len(a.location), 0)                                                    AS n_stops
FROM al

-- Server side: one row per alert and route it names, for the route filter.
WITH feed AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT from_json((SELECT content FROM read_text('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/alerts')),
                   '{"resultSet": {"alert": [{"id": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR", "begin": "BIGINT", "system_wide_flag": "BOOLEAN", "route": [{"route": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR"}], "location": [{"id": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR", "lat": "DOUBLE", "lng": "DOUBLE"}]}]}}').resultSet AS rs
),
al AS (SELECT unnest(rs.alert) AS a FROM feed)
SELECT DISTINCT a.id, r."desc" AS route
FROM (SELECT a, unnest(a.route) AS r FROM al)

-- Server side: one row per alert and stop it names, drawn as rings on the map.
WITH feed AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT from_json((SELECT content FROM read_text('http://feeds/trimet/ws/v2/alerts')),
                   '{"resultSet": {"alert": [{"id": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR", "begin": "BIGINT", "system_wide_flag": "BOOLEAN", "route": [{"route": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR"}], "location": [{"id": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR", "lat": "DOUBLE", "lng": "DOUBLE"}]}]}}').resultSet AS rs
),
al AS (SELECT unnest(rs.alert) AS a FROM feed)
SELECT a.id,
       trim(a."desc", chr(10) || ' ')                                                  AS alert,
       array_to_string(list_sort(list_distinct(list_transform(a.route, x -> x."desc"))), ', ') AS affects,
       l."desc"                                                                        AS stop,
       l.lat                                                                           AS latitude,
       l.lng                                                                           AS longitude
FROM (SELECT a, unnest(a.location) AS l FROM al)

-- Server side, once per visit: every route, one row per direction, drawn stop
-- to stop from the route configuration rather than along the street (the
-- street geometry lives in the GTFS zip, whose shapes take ~17 s to read).
-- Also the Route variable's list, in TriMet's own order.
WITH rcs AS (SELECT unnest(from_json((SELECT content FROM read_text('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true&dir=true&stops=true')),
                         '{"resultSet": {"route": [{"route": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR", "routeSubType": "VARCHAR", "routeColor": "VARCHAR", "routeSortOrder": "BIGINT", "dir": [{"dir": "BIGINT", "stop": [{"locid": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR", "lat": "DOUBLE", "lng": "DOUBLE", "seq": "BIGINT"}]}]}]}}').resultSet.route) AS r),
st AS (
  SELECT r.route AS num, r."desc" AS route, r.routeSubType AS subtype, r.routeColor AS hex,
         r.routeSortOrder AS sort_order, d.dir, unnest(d.stop) AS s
  FROM (SELECT r, unnest(r.dir) AS d FROM rcs)
)
SELECT num,
       route,
       CASE subtype WHEN 'Light Rail' THEN 'MAX light rail' WHEN 'BRT' THEN 'FX bus rapid transit' WHEN 'Commuter Rail' THEN 'WES commuter rail' WHEN 'Streetcar' THEN 'Streetcar' WHEN 'Aerial Tram' THEN 'Aerial tram' ELSE 'Bus' END AS mode,
       sort_order,
       dir,
       '#' || coalesce(hex, '4679AA')                                 AS color,
       CASE subtype WHEN 'Bus' THEN 1 WHEN 'BRT' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END     AS width,
       '{"type":"LineString","coordinates":[' ||
         string_agg('[' || s.lng || ',' || s.lat || ']', ',' ORDER BY s.seq) || ']}' AS geojson
FROM st
GROUP BY ALL
HAVING count(*) > 1

-- Server side, once per visit: every stop with its name and position, from
-- the route configuration. A stop served by several routes is listed once.
WITH rcs AS (SELECT unnest(from_json((SELECT content FROM read_text('http://feeds/trimet/ws/V1/routeConfig?json=true&dir=true&stops=true')),
                         '{"resultSet": {"route": [{"route": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR", "routeSubType": "VARCHAR", "routeColor": "VARCHAR", "routeSortOrder": "BIGINT", "dir": [{"dir": "BIGINT", "stop": [{"locid": "BIGINT", "desc": "VARCHAR", "lat": "DOUBLE", "lng": "DOUBLE", "seq": "BIGINT"}]}]}]}}').resultSet.route) AS r),
s AS (SELECT unnest(d.stop) AS s FROM (SELECT unnest(r.dir) AS d FROM rcs))
SELECT s.locid,
       any_value(s."desc") AS name,
       any_value(s.lat)    AS lat,
       any_value(s.lng)    AS lng
FROM s
GROUP BY 1

spec.sql:
-- Every route TriMet publishes, within the modes picked, in TriMet's order.
SELECT route FROM (
  SELECT route, min(sort_order) AS sort_order FROM $routes
  WHERE mode IN (${mode:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY route
)
ORDER BY sort_order
